# UKIP 2010 Manifesto Summary

The UK Independence Party's 2010 manifesto centers on one core objective: withdrawing Britain from the European Union to restore national sovereignty, save money, and reclaim democratic control.

## Key Arguments for Leaving the EU

UKIP claims EU membership costs Britain £6.4 billion annually in net contributions (rising to £10 billion), with indirect costs like regulation potentially reaching £120 billion yearly. The party argues that 72% of business regulations originate from Brussels, with over 120,000 EU directives affecting British life. They dispute claims that three million jobs depend on EU membership, noting that European companies sell more to Britain than vice versa.

## Economic Policies

UKIP proposes radical tax simplification, including a 31% flat tax starting at £11,500 (taking minimum wage earners out of tax entirely), phasing out employers' National Insurance over five years, and replacing VAT with a Local Sales Tax. They advocate reducing public sector employment to 1997 levels and abolishing inheritance tax. For banking reform, they propose returning oversight to the Bank of England and separating retail from investment banking.

## Immigration

The manifesto calls for an immediate five-year freeze on permanent immigration, followed by an Australian-style points system. UKIP would triple border staff to 30,000, refuse amnesty for illegal immigrants, and require asylum seekers to be held in secure centres during processing. They would repeal the Human Rights Act and withdraw from the European Convention on Human Rights.

## Public Services

For the NHS, UKIP proposes elected County Health Boards, abolishing bureaucratic layers, and introducing Health Credit Vouchers for those preferring private healthcare. In education, they support School Vouchers enabling parental choice, grammar school expansion, and scrapping the 50% university attendance target. The pension system would be simplified into a non-means-tested Citizen's Pension of at least £130 weekly.

## Defence and Foreign Policy

UKIP pledges a 40% increase in defence spending, expanding the Army by 25%, restoring the Royal Navy, and maintaining nuclear deterrents. They propose establishing a Commonwealth Free Trade Area and negotiating Swiss-style trade agreements with Europe while regaining Britain's WTO seat.

## Energy and Environment

The party takes a sceptical stance on man-made climate change, calling for repeal of the Climate Change Act, increased nuclear power to 50% of electricity needs, and opposition to wind farms. They would withdraw from EU carbon trading schemes.

## Constitutional Reform

UKIP advocates direct democracy through binding referendums (triggered by 5% of the electorate), proportional representation via Alternative Vote Plus, directly elected local boards for police, health, and education, and abolition of regional government. They support devolved assemblies but would replace their members with existing Westminster MPs.

## Social Issues

The manifesto promotes "uniculturalism" over multiculturalism, proposes banning the burqa in public buildings, making St George's Day a public holiday, and allowing local referendums on hunting. UKIP supports designated smoking rooms in pubs and protecting the Post Office network.

The manifesto presents EU withdrawal as the solution to virtually every policy challenge, promising that reclaimed sovereignty and saved contributions would fund improvements across all public services.
